prediction.likelyOutcome: Montgomery Park has a moderately favorable but genuinely contested path to a rent judgment against NCO — the tenant vacated and stopped paying despite an express pre-vacatur landlord notice disputing satisfaction of the termination conditions, which is a weak evidentiary posture for a tenant claiming valid self-termination. On the numbers actually in the record, MP's recoverable rent floor is the $313,662.76 stated in the July 2011 default letter, with materially larger exposure (additional accrued rent through the original lease term, default-rate interest, and contractual attorneys' fees) likely but not quantifiable from the facts provided.

issues.label: NCO's Overcharge, Unjust Enrichment and Fraud Claims

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court entered judgment for Montgomery Park on its past-due-rent counterclaim of $9,854,566.95 plus postjudgment interest (upheld in earlier Fourth Circuit appeals at 842 F.3d 816, 918 F.3d 388 and 40 F.4th 123). The court then awarded $2,074,379.88 in attorneys' fees and nontaxable expenses, $115,942.10 taxable costs and $1,576,036.07 default interest ($3,766,358.05 total). In this fifth appeal the Fourth Circuit affirmed the fee/cost award (including expert fees) but vacated the default-interest component, holding interest runs only from the August 24, 2022 demand, and remanded for recalculation; the underlying rent judgment was not disturbed.
